ideas.title: GeoNerd: AI visibility digest for UK accountancy practices

why_now.changed: AI assistants became a mainstream surface for local service discovery (ChatGPT at scale from late 2023; Google AI Overviews rolled out from May 2024), creating an AI-visibility question for professional-services buyers that did not exist three years ago.
why_now.why_it_matters: The shift creates a new monitoring job for practices; without it this would not have been an attractive business three years ago.
why_now.competitors_responded: Yes - TendorAI, Tramwai (£299/mo), AireStream and SearchScore already sell AI visibility to UK accountants, which weakens the wedge but does not remove the category shift.

fingerprint.buyer: UK accountancy practices, 1-20 staff, owner/partner decision maker; first beachhead contractor/IR35 specialists
fingerprint.problem: Practices cannot see whether AI assistants recommend them when local business owners ask for an accountant, who is recommended instead, or why
fingerprint.mechanism: Free domain-in AI visibility scan plus a £19.99/mo plain-language monthly digest of visibility changes and prioritised actions

ideas.title: ShiftSwap: last-minute shift cover for UK hospitality

why_now.changed: None identified: shift-cover functionality is a long-standing commodity already bundled into low-cost UK rota products.
why_now.why_it_matters: Without a discontinuity the idea is a me-too variant competing on price against bundled features; under method 1.1.0 that is a strong reason to reject at screening.
why_now.competitors_responded: Yes - rota incumbents at £0-£49/mo already include self-service shift swaps.

fingerprint.buyer: Small UK hospitality venue owners/GMs (1-5 sites); duty managers and hourly staff as users
fingerprint.problem: Last-minute absences leave shifts uncovered, forcing managers to phone around or close sections
fingerprint.mechanism: Standalone shift-cover app/marketplace where staff offer and claim shifts, with manager approval

why_now.changed: None identified: surplus-produce subscriptions have been operated at scale by Oddbox since 2018 and its financials show category economics have not improved.
why_now.why_it_matters: No regulatory, technical or platform change improves local delivery economics; the incumbent's widening losses are the relevant evidence.
why_now.competitors_responded: Yes - Oddbox and Wonky Veg Boxes occupy the position; Oddbox's revenue fell after it cut new-customer marketing.

fingerprint.buyer: Food-waste-conscious UK households buying a weekly grocery box
fingerprint.problem: Odd-shaped and surplus produce goes to waste while households want affordable fresh food
fingerprint.mechanism: Local weekly surplus-produce box subscription at roughly £10-£18 per box, delivered or collected

ideas.title: GrantScout: matched UK grant digest for small businesses

why_now.changed: No favourable discontinuity: GOV.UK 'Find a grant' already provides authoritative free discovery and the flat-fee paid position was already occupied (GovOwed) before this run.
why_now.why_it_matters: Absent a discontinuity the digest competes with a free authoritative service and contingency-priced incumbents; the observed value shift was toward application quality, not discovery (see seeds/grantscout-application-quality.md).
why_now.competitors_responded: Yes - GOV.UK Find a grant (free), GovOwed (£29 one-time / £499 per year) and contingency-priced advisers.

fingerprint.buyer: UK SME owners/directors, or their accountants and advisers
fingerprint.problem: Eligible grant schemes are hard to find and interpret, and missing funding is a direct loss
fingerprint.mechanism: Monthly matched grant digest (£15-£29/mo) with plain-language eligibility and deadlines

why_now.changed: OpenAI and Stripe launched ACP/Instant Checkout on 29 September 2025 and Shopify and Google published UCP; agent-mediated discovery and checkout became a live platform surface and the major platforms now bundle readiness for it.
why_now.why_it_matters: The change creates a genuine new integration job, but it is adverse to a standalone wedge: the parties that opened the surface give readiness away inside their standard offer.
why_now.competitors_responded: Yes - Shopify/Google (UCP), OpenAI/Stripe (ACP), PayPal, WooCommerce, BigCommerce and Salesforce are all shipping, bundling readiness at no incremental fee.

fingerprint.buyer: Independent/off-platform e-commerce merchants and their agencies
fingerprint.problem: Merchants are not ready for agent-mediated discovery and checkout and may lose agent-driven sales
fingerprint.mechanism: Guided product-feed preparation plus ACP/UCP checkout integration service/tooling

ideas.title: PPWR packaging compliance for small UK brands and exporters

why_now.changed: Regulation (EU) 2025/40 (PPWR) generally applies from 12 August 2026, adding PFAS limits in food-contact packaging, traceability/labelling, technical documentation, importer Declaration of Conformity retention and per-Member-State EPR registration for packaged goods placed on the EU market.
why_now.why_it_matters: A hard, dated EU-wide duty for a large population of brand owners and importers did not exist in this form three years ago.
why_now.competitors_responded: Yes - PPWR Copilot (UK, GBP49-499/mo), PPWRify, PPWR Connect and Trace One (marketing to 9,000+ brands) already sell PPWR workflows.

fingerprint.buyer: Small UK packaged-goods brands and importers selling into the EU, and their agents
fingerprint.problem: New PPWR labelling, Declaration of Conformity and EPR duties with per-country variation are confusing and time-bound
fingerprint.mechanism: Guided packaging dossier plus QR label and EU Declaration of Conformity generator

ideas.title: "All reasonable steps": harassment-prevention evidence for UK SMEs

why_now.changed: The Employment Rights Act 2025 (c.36) raises the preventive duty to 'all reasonable steps' (Equality Act 2010 s.40A) and adds a third-party harassment duty from 30 October 2026, with liability unless all reasonable steps were taken.
why_now.why_it_matters: Both the standard of proof and the scope of the duty tighten on a fixed date, creating a new evidence/record-keeping job for employers that did not exist in this form before.
why_now.competitors_responded: Partially - free Acas/EHRC guidance and paid generic training exist and HR platforms cover adjacent needs; no dedicated low-cost SME evidence tool was surfaced.

fingerprint.buyer: UK SME employers with roughly 10-100 staff, no dedicated HR system, owner or office manager handling HR
fingerprint.problem: Employers must be able to evidence 'all reasonable steps' and that they did not permit third-party harassment from 30 October 2026, with no system of record
fingerprint.mechanism: Low-cost (GBP12-20/mo) 'all reasonable steps' evidence toolkit: guided risk assessment, incident log, policy acknowledgement and training records, exportable evidence pack
